text:
maria: quick flag 1: our new node sample using kue doesn't keep the X-Req-Id through to the worker. worker logs show a fresh id.

leah: that's bad for tracing. which OTEL lib are you using?

maria: @leah standard @opentelemetry/sdk-node + auto-instrumentations, and a tiny req-id middleware: ```js
app.use((req,res,next) => { const id = req.headers['x-request-id'] || uuid.v4(); req.requestId = id; res.setHeader('X-Request-Id', id); next(); });
```
we push a job with job.data but didn't attach meta. I assumed context propagation would survive the queue boundary.

jordan: queues almost always break process-local context. Python/celery hit around this by serializing traceparent into the task headers. Have you tried adding traceparent/request-id into job.data?

maria: not yet. i'm thinking the SDK should offer a helper so samples don't reinvent it. same problem cropped up for our go SDK sample yesterday (different queue lib).

sam: agree. proposal: sdk-js export `enqueueWithContext(queue, job, ctx)` that injects traceparent + X-Request-Id into job.meta. also add `restoreContextFromJob(job)` for worker bootstrap.

ian: also note env-level behavior: our k8s ingress strips unknown headers unless you set `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/configuration-snippet` to forward them, or add them to `proxy_set_header`. I'll update infra docs. Example snippet: ```nginx
proxy_set_header X-Request-Id $http_x_request_id;
proxy_set_header traceparent $http_traceparent;
```
without this, even HTTP -> queue -> worker won't preserve the id.

leah: thanks. another gap: debug logs currently skip scrubbing of secrets in the node SDK. folks have seen API keys in debug output during local runs. we need a sample-safe flag: `LOG_DEBUG_SAFE=true` so debug still redacts tokens.

sam: i can add both: the enqueue helper and a small config toggle that activates the scrubber for DEBUG. will add unit tests and a small perf microbenchmark.

maria: can we also add an e2e to the sample-apps repo that: (1) issues an HTTP request, (2) enqueues a job, (3) asserts worker stdout contains same X-Request-Id? would catch regressions.

jordan: yes, keep it lightweight. use a fake worker in CI that returns the id in a JSON blob. e2e job should timeout fast if missing.

leah: on redaction implementation: recommend scanning for 40+ char hex strings, bearer tokens, and the header keys we consider secrets. sample scrubber pseudo: ```js
function scrub(msg) { return msg.replace(/(Bearer\s+[A-Za-z0-9\-_.]+)/g, '[REDACTED]') }
```
we'll refine.

sam: open issue to track: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/issues/450 1. will attach PR once helper lives.

maria: created a WIP sample PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sample-apps/pull/240 1 (adds a queue-context helper + debug-safe env). cc @sam for helper follow-up.

ian: i'll add ingress note to infra docs and a short troubleshooting checklist: "missing X-Request-Id? check ingress, proxy, and job meta".

jordan: also add test matrices to ensure parity between node/python/go samples for: enqueue, restore, and redaction behavior. parity tests can be tiny scripts.

devex-bot: CI | sample-apps PR 240 1 1 checks queued: lint, telemetry-e2e, integration.

sam: thanks everyone. i'll take the sdk helper + tests. @leah can you prototype the scrubber and share perf numbers?

leah: yep, will bench and post numbers in the PR. initial run looks negligible on throughput.

maria: leaving this thread open for follow-ups. ping if you want to pair on the sample changes.
